title: Error handling and context managers
summary: try / except / else / finally handles errors: else runs if there was no exception and finally always runs.

sections.definition: try / except / else / finally handles errors: else runs if there was no exception and finally always runs. Custom exceptions inherit from Exception. A context manager (with) guarantees setup and cleanup, through __enter__/__exit__ or the @contextmanager decorator.
sections.analogy: The with is signing out the storeroom keys: whatever happens inside, when you leave you return the keys.
sections.problem: Swallowing errors hides bugs and leaves data half-done. Without with, an error midway leaves files open or transactions unclosed.
sections.code:example:
class StockInsuficiente(Exception):
    def __init__(self, producto: str, pedido: int, disponible: int):
        super().__init__(f"{producto}: pediste {pedido}, hay {disponible}")
        self.producto = producto

def reservar(producto: str, cantidad: int) -> None:
    disponible = stock.get(producto, 0)
    if cantidad > disponible:
        raise StockInsuficiente(producto, cantidad, disponible)
    stock[producto] -= cantidad

try:
    reservar("cafe", 50)
except StockInsuficiente as e:
    print("No se pudo:", e)
else:
    print("Reservado")
finally:
    print("Fin del intento")

from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def transaccion(sesion):
    try:
        yield sesion
        sesion.commit()
    except Exception:
        sesion.rollback()
        raise
sections.bad:
try:
    reservar("cafe", 50)
except:
    pass

It catches everything, even Ctrl+C (KeyboardInterrupt), and nobody finds out about the failure.
sections.good:
try:
    reservar("cafe", 50)
except StockInsuficiente as e:
    logger.warning("Sin stock: %s", e)
    raise ErrorDePedido("No se pudo reservar") from e

You catch what you expect and keep the original cause with from e.
sections.bridge:typescript: try/catch/finally ≈ try/except/finally; throw → raise; catch (e) → except Tipo as e. with has no classic equivalent in JS; the closest is using (explicit resource management, TS 5.2+). Python prefers the EAFP style: try and catch, instead of checking everything beforehand.
sections.interview: I catch specific exceptions, never a bare except. I use else for code that should only run if there was no error and finally for mandatory cleanup. For business errors I create custom exceptions that inherit from Exception, and I chain causes with raise from. For resources like files, connections or transactions I use context managers with with, which guarantee release even if there's an exception.
sections.myths:
• A bare except: without a type also catches SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt.
  • Not knowing the try's else: it separates the code that can fail from the code that only runs if everything went well.
  • Re-raising with raise e instead of a bare raise changes the traceback's point of origin.
  • Inheriting from BaseException instead of Exception.

items.code:
try:
    print(1)
    x = 1 / 0
    print(2)
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print(3)
else:
    print(4)
finally:
    print(5)
items.why: The 2 never runs; else is skipped because there was an exception; finally always runs.

items.q: What does with open("pedidos.csv") as f: guarantee?
options: That it's closed when leaving the block, even on error
items.why: The context manager always calls __exit__, and that's where the file is closed.
